lens: Skeptical solo indie dev with limited calendar time, attacking scope realism, sequencing and true critical path. Verified against the repo, not the brief: PersistenceKeys is 8 frozen keys asserted by value in storage.test.ts; jest.config.js collects only src/**/__tests__/**/*.test.ts in node env (no .tsx, and no src/core/__tests__/saveSystem.test.ts exists although four steps verify against it); grep for ReduceMotion and AppState across src/ each return 0; blockerOpacityAt(1)=0 and blockedBumpAt(1)=0 confirmed by reading src/ui/feedbackCurves.ts; Difficulties.config(d) is a switch on tier with no level index; ShapeLibrary.pick is the first RNG consumer in LevelGenerator.generate so W4-02's shapeNameFor premise holds for v1; and GameScreen only ever calls SaveSystem.setCurrentLevel on a clear, so no mid-level board state is persisted at all. HEADLINE: this is a strong audit wearing a plan's clothes. The findings are real and mostly well-evidenced. The PLAN, as a schedule, has four structural faults. (1) DUPLICATION: the same work is written three or four times across workstreams under different ids — TEST AD strip (W0-01 = W7-03), initAds restructure (W0-01/W0-05 + W6-06 + W7-01 all rewrite one function), contrast test (W0-07 = W5-02, two different filenames), eas projectId (W0-08 = W7-10), reduce-motion (W0-03 subsumed by W2-02, via a DIFFERENT mechanism, unreconciled), ad pacing (W0-06 superseded by W7-11), and THREE separate screen-capture harnesses (W2-01, W5-01, W6-11+W6-13). A solo dev executing this in order builds each of these twice. (2) UNOWNED SHARED RESOURCE: five workstreams (W0-06, W1-03, W3-01, W4-01, W6-03) each independently append to the same Object.freeze'd PersistenceKeys and each rewrites the same exact-array assertion, each calling that assertion "the intended tripwire". They cannot merge in any order without conflict, and W4-01's acceptance ("exactly 19 entries") is arithmetically wrong the moment any other one lands first. W4-01 and W6-03 both define arrows_schema_version, with different migration semantics. (3) THE CAPTURE INSTRUMENT IS UNCALIBRATED AND LOAD-BEARING: eleven of twelve W2 steps close on "a W2-01 capture shows at least N frames", while W6-13 in the same plan states that adb screenrecord steals frames on a software-GPU emulator and forbids quoting timing from a recorded run. Counting frames on a recorder whose effective frame rate was never established is a percentile over an unverified sample count — the exact scar this project has hit four times. (4) THE PRODUCT ISN'T THE BOTTLENECK THE PLAN THINKS: W2 (feel) and W5 (art) are ~26 steps of polish on a game whose measured failure is that a new player loses three hearts in six taps having never been told the rule. No amount of overlay easing retains someone who quit in the first 90 seconds. TRUE CRITICAL PATH: land the uncommitted working tree -> verify targetSdk 36 and eas projectId (a shippable-at-all check, ~30 min) -> one consolidated persistence-schema step -> W0 defects -> W1 FTUE -> W7-02 GATE 0 spike -> daily board -> difficulty curve. Everything else is downstream or optional.

kills.reason: Secretly XL sold as M, and its justification is weaker than the author believes. It creates a PERMANENT byte-identical fork of levelGenerator.ts, difficulty.ts and shapeLibrary.ts into src/core/generation/v1/, maintained forever, plus dual checksum tables, plus a version argument threaded into generate-promo-art.ts and soak-plan.ts, plus two new persisted keys. The stated harm it prevents is a player force-quitting mid-level and reopening to a different board. But I verified in GameScreen.tsx that SaveSystem.setCurrentLevel is only ever called on a clear and nothing persists mid-level board state: that player ALREADY loses all progress on that board and restarts it from scratch. The delta is 'the board I have to restart looks different' — much smaller than the fork's carrying cost. I attacked this: the real harm is not the force-quit, it is that an existing level-40 player on a flat ~96-arrow game would suddenly jump onto a ramp that may hand them a much EASIER board mid-campaign, a visible regression with no crash reporting to detect it. That case wins on the harm and loses on the mechanism.
kills.replacement: Keep the guarantee, drop the fork. One persisted int (the switch level) plus a monotone floor in targetArrows so an existing player's board count can never drop below what v1 gave them at that index. Zero duplicated modules, one checksum table, one shape library, no version argument anywhere. If the owner will accept board substitution at the next level boundary, even that int disappears.

kills.reason: This is the single load-bearing instrument for eleven other steps and it is marked M. It must set animator scales to 1 and assert readback (which is W6-11), run screenrecord around a scripted phase and split frames (which is W6-13's --record), and reach non-PERF_MODE screens (which is W5-01's capture-device.mjs). Three workstreams build this. Worse, W6-13 in the same plan states screenrecord steals frames on a software-GPU emulator and therefore forces runs=1 and stamps perfNumbersInvalid — yet every W2 acceptance criterion is a COUNT OF FRAMES from exactly that recorder ('at least three consecutive frames', W2-06's 'difference is at least 3 recorded frames'). A 300 ms effect is 18 frames at 60 fps but may be 4 at the recorder's real rate; nobody has established that rate.
kills.replacement: Build ONE capture harness, once, merging W2-01 + W5-01 + W6-11 + W6-13's --record. Its first acceptance criterion must be the reconciliation this project's own rules demand: record a known-duration effect and print observed frames vs window x measured recorder rate. Until that number exists, no step may state a frame-count threshold — restate W2's criteria as 'the effect is visible in the recording' plus owner eyeball, which is what actually closes feel work anyway.

kills.reason: Its acceptance criterion 'SaveSystem.persistenceKeys has exactly 19 entries' is 8 + W4's own 11, computed as if W4 were the only workstream touching the array. W0-06 adds arrows_finished_games, W1-03 adds arrows_ftue_stage, W3-01 adds two gen keys, and W6-03 adds arrows_schema_version — which W4-01 ALSO adds, with different migration semantics. Five workstreams each mutate one Object.freeze'd array and each rewrites the same by-value assertion in storage.test.ts (verified: it asserts all 8 strings literally), and each describes that assertion failing as its own intended tripwire. In any merge order, four of the five break, and the count is wrong.
kills.replacement: One consolidated persistence-schema step, executed FIRST, that lands every key the whole plan will ever need (schema version, ftue stage, finished games, daily triple, shields, shapes bitmask, notif, review, gen version) in one frozen array with one migration and one updated assertion. Downstream steps then only add getters. Also resolve the duplicate arrows_schema_version definition between W4-01 and W6-03 to a single owner.

kills.reason: The first-level gate is unsatisfiable by the step's own measurements. It requires level 1 to have blockedTaps <= 5 AND clearable >= 45%, and pins A_start to the 21-38 arrow range. The cited sensitivity table gives Circle at 12 rows = 21 arrows / 54.4% clearable / 9 expected blocked taps, and at 16 rows = 38 arrows / 38.3% / 32. The FLOOR of the specified A_start range already measures 9 blocked taps, so no value in 21-38 arrows can reach 5. This is the unfillable-goal pattern that has fired repeatedly on this codebase. Separately, tau is 'fitted numerically' to two constraints (reach v1's band by level 30, within 5% of asymptote by level 400) whose 30, 400, +/-15% and 5% are all invented — a fit to invented endpoints launders an invented number into a measured-sounding one.
kills.replacement: Run the probe (W3-02) BELOW 12 rows first and read the actual blocked-tap curve, then set the gate to a value the measurement can reach; or state the gate as a delta ('at least 5x fewer expected blocked taps than v1 level 1's measured 82') which is falsifiable without pinning an unreachable absolute. Label the tau endpoints explicitly as design choices, not measurements.

kills.reason: Two faults. First, zero margin: the acceptance asserts min slack >= band height + 15 dp, the band is capped at 96 dp, and the measured worst case on 360x780 is 111 dp. 96 + 15 = 111 exactly. Any device or header variation puts a band over a drawn arrow, which is the one thing 'the board is sacred' forbids. Second, and worse, the slack numbers were computed from an ASSUMED header of 'approx 76 dp' — while W1-01 in the same plan exists precisely because that viewport is produced by React Native layout after the header and safe-area insets and 'is NOT derivable from any config file'. Two workstreams disagree about whether this number can be computed.
kills.replacement: Take W1-01's logged onLayout viewport as the input, on all three geometries, before choosing a band height; then set the band to leave a stated margin (not zero) against the logged worst case. If the logged slack does not support a 96 dp band, shrink the band rather than the margin.

Every perf claim in the plan: one API 31 emulator, software GPU, no physical device on any platform, host Mac load already proven to make absolute gates unevaluable once (docs/perf-tap-forgiveness-ab-2026-09-08.md).

Those are trust defects; every other investment in this plan is worthless if the app looks fake or hangs. W1 survives because it is the only workstream aimed at the largest MEASURED leak: a new player loses three hearts in six taps on a 60-arrow board where 32% of arrows are clearable, having never been told the rule, and grep for tutorial|onboard|first.?run returns 0 hits. W0-03 survives inside W1's blast radius because I confirmed blockerOpacityAt(1) = 0 and blockedBumpAt(1) = 0 in feedbackCurves.ts — with OS reduce motion on, the game's only explanation of its core rule renders literally nothing, which makes the entire FTUE lesson invisible to that player. W4-03/W4-05 survive because the deterministic generator makes a date-seeded daily nearly free (seed by day instead of level counter) and it is the load-bearing retention system every competitor in this genre ships. W3-02/W3-04/W3-06 survive because difficulty is provably flat forever (Difficulties.config is a switch on tier with no level index — I read it) and 33% of levels are a plain rectangle; W3-06's bag fixes the variety with zero new art, which is why it survives and W3-08 does not. All twelve W2 steps: their acceptance model is frame-counting on an instrument the same plan says steals frames, and no amount of overlay easing retains a player who quit in the first ninety seconds. Thirteen of fourteen W5 steps: real gaps, but icons and a vectorised wordmark are not survival, and W5-04 is blocked on an unanswered brand escalation anyway. Thirteen of fourteen W6 steps: telemetry is genuinely the thing that makes everything else falsifiable — and that is precisely the argument I want to attack. NOW I ATTACK MY OWN CUT, TWICE. First attack: 'instrumentation makes everything else falsifiable, so W6 must come first, and cutting it means shipping W1/W3/W4 blind with no way to know whether any of it worked.' That case is strong and it partially wins — it defeats my blanket cut of W6, and it is why W6-08 and the capture-harness consolidation stay in. It does NOT win overall, because W6 is ~14 steps including a first-party ingest endpoint, a privacy-policy rewrite, a Data safety reconciliation, a crash pipeline and a two-project jest migration whose dependencies are unverified — that is the largest workstream in the plan, aimed at measuring a product that currently kills new players in six taps. Measure second; stop the bleeding first. Second attack, and the one I take most seriously: 'W3-01 must stay, because without the version seam an existing level-40 player jumps from a flat ~96-arrow board onto a ramp that may hand them a much easier one mid-campaign — a silent regression with no crash reporting to catch it.' That case wins on the HARM and loses on the MECHANISM, which is why my verdict on W3-01 is REWORK rather than CUT: keep the guarantee via one persisted switch level plus a monotone floor on targetArrows, and refuse the permanent byte-identical fork of three core modules with dual checksum tables and a version argument threaded through the promo-art and soak scripts. My original instinct — 'cut it, because a force-quit already discards mid-level progress, which I verified by confirming setCurrentLevel fires only on a clear' — was too aggressive, and I am dropping that half of the objection.
